overview.oneLineTake: Fade the comfort of Monday's bounce: 5% yields, $109 Brent and a heavy earnings slate keep event vol bid, so sell premium only with defined risk and size down into Tesla and Meta.
themes: Relief bounce, not a reset. QQQ rose 1.2% Monday to 718.36 and SPY gained 0.4% to 766.48 as Micron, Intel and the chip complex snapped back from tech's worst selling week in five years, but volume was thin and the Dow slipped below its 50-day line.
Positioning is washed out in tech. Goldman says hedge funds cut tech at the fastest pace in a decade, which fuels sharp squeezes but leaves the bounce dependent on earnings to hold.
Rates are still the ceiling. The 10-year sits at 5.09% after hot September CPI and PPI, hike talk is live again, and Treasuries sold off as haven demand faded with the tech rebound.
Oil risk is escalating. Brent topped $109 after Houthi claims of attacks on Saudi airports and Aramco sites, and Saudi Arabia pushed its FII investor conference to 2027.
Earnings week is the test. Tesla, Meta and SpaceX report into a tape where Wells Fargo says most early reporters have fallen short.
risks: Further Gulf escalation pushing Brent above $110 and feeding hike odds.
Megacap earnings misses breaking the chip bounce while positioning rebuilds.
Junk credit stress widening, with the riskiest high yield bonds already flashing a warning.
French unrest hitting Paris stocks, bonds and the euro.

intelligence.headline: US Stock Futures Rise After Last Week's Chip Rout
intelligence.summary: US stock futures are rising, offering investors some respite from last week's rout in semiconductor stocks.

intelligence.headline: French Stocks and Bonds Slump as Rioting Pressures Government
intelligence.summary: After a weekend of violent unrest over the cost of living, France's 10-year yield is up 8 basis points to 4.88%, among the highest in Western Europe, and its premium over German bunds has widened further into territory associated with the euro-area debt crisis. The CAC 40 is the worst-performing European index, down 3.7% this year while the Stoxx Europe 600 has gained 8.1%.

intelligence.headline: French Violence Raises Alert as Protests Flare Across Europe
intelligence.summary: Heavy debt and one of the euro area's largest deficits leave France unable to spend its way out of the unrest, and Parliament must pass a 2027 budget with spending cuts and higher taxes in the coming weeks, with a presidential election six months away.

intelligence.headline: Nscale Faces Investor Pushback Over IPO Valuation
intelligence.summary: Nvidia-backed data-center developer Nscale faces investor opposition to the $30 billion valuation it is pursuing in its IPO after a series of market setbacks for AI companies.

intelligence.headline: Anthropic Plans to Shift 5% of Shares Into Public Good Fund
intelligence.summary: Anthropic said it plans to put 5% of its shares into a fund that will be used to address the public good.

intelligence.headline: Musk Says He Will Gift SpaceX Shares to Every Kid in America
intelligence.summary: Elon Musk pledged to distribute a share of SpaceX to each American child; it is not clear how the contributions would work and he did not elaborate.

intelligence.headline: On the Move: French Stocks Hit, Chips Rally, Intel Upgraded
intelligence.summary: Accor fell 3.4%, Stellantis 4.5% and LVMH 2.3% after the riots. Premarket chip gains: Nvidia +1.5%, Marvell 3.4%, AMD 2.7%, Broadcom 2.4%. Intel rose 4.2% on a JPMorgan upgrade to neutral, and Boyd Gaming 1.9% on a Morgan Stanley upgrade to overweight.

intelligence.headline: The Week Ahead: Earnings Pick Up Pace
intelligence.summary: Earnings: Fifth Third (Mon); SpaceX, Netflix, GE, Northrop Grumman, GM, KeyCorp, United Airlines, ABB (Tue); Tesla, Meta, Abbott, AT&T, IBM, Texas Instruments, SAP (Wed); Blackstone, Honeywell, Lockheed Martin, American Airlines (Thu); American Express (Fri). Housing starts and pending home sales Tuesday, S&P Global October PMIs Friday.

intelligence.headline: Option Traders Brace for VIX Surge as AI Jitters Jolt Market
intelligence.summary: The S&P 500 had gone 53 sessions without a 1% drop, the longest stretch since January 2020, before falling more than 1% on both Wednesday and Friday as expected volatility jumped on doubts about the AI boom.

intelligence.headline: Bond Market's Big Short Bet Gets Wakeup Call as AI Trade Wobbles
intelligence.summary: AI anxiety is helping US Treasuries reclaim their haven role; State Street's Masahiko Loo said Treasuries increasingly look capable of hedging a bigger AI-driven risk-off episode.

intelligence.headline: The Fate of Warren Buffett's $150 Billion Fortune
intelligence.summary: Buffett's $150 billion fortune will be decided by three very different siblings living three very different lives.

intelligence.headline: US Interest Costs Hit Record $1.05 Trillion
intelligence.summary: Annual US net interest costs reached a record $1.05 trillion in the year through September, up more than 8% from the prior year, reflecting more debt and higher rates.
